title: Console debug KV-cache & fallback playbook - HarborCare
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked HarborCare through the Console debugging playbook: how to trace request chains, use Request Inspector playback for root-cause, interpret KV cache hits/misses, and configure graceful fallback model variants. Discussion covered dedicated vs hosted implications for lat and compliance, and next steps to run a short perf pilot and review security artifacts.
next_steps: Redwood: share SOC2 + network diagrams + KMS integration doc (due 2025-10-10)
HarborCare: provide 2 sample failing trace IDs and a small prompt set for repro testing (due 2025-10-13)
Schedule 1-hour pilot kickoff for private/VPC trial (proposed window: week of 2025-10-20)
Diego to spin up a 1-hour live playback session showing request replay and kv cache tuning (by 2025-10-14)
action_items: Aisha Rahman; Send pricing + dedicated capacity quote; 2025-10-11
Diego Morales; Prepare playback demo env and scripts; 2025-10-14
Tom Nguyen; Gather three problematic trace IDs and attach logs; 2025-10-13

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Rahman (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (HarborCare Eng Mgr), Tom Nguyen (HarborCare SRE), Elena Rossi (HarborCare Head of Data), Jared Lee (HarborCare Security), Priya Desai (HarborCare Product)

Summary (auto): quick Console walkthrough focusing on tracing, request playback, kv cache hits/misses, and fallback configuration. Action items captured at end.

00:00 - Aisha: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate it. quick roll call?
00:12 - Maya: maya here, tom, elena and jared from my side.
00:16 - Tom: yep tom.
00:18 - Aisha: perfect, i'll hand to diego to jump into the console. diego, over to you.
00:23 - Diego: thanks aisha. so i'll share my screen, i'm in the Redwood Console; i'll open Request Inspector which is under Observability > Requests. you can see a list of recent requests, each has a trace id, status, model, and latency breakdown.
00:40 - Priya: is that the same view we get on Hosted? we want parity between hosted and dedicated.
00:46 - Diego: yes, that's by design. the Console shows the same traces whether Hosted or Dedicated - with the caveat that for Private/VPC we surface additional network metadata. but the request shape and token-level timing are consistent.
01:02 - Diego: i'll click a failing request — trace id 4f9b-2c7a — and open the waterfall. notice the colored spans: parsing, context fetch, kv-cache lookup, model inference, token stream. here you can see a big gap around the kv-cache lookup.
01:23 - Elena: that gap — is that a miss or are we seeing network retry?
01:27 - Diego: good q. the span shows an explicit miss: kvcache.lookup -> miss then backend fetch. our Console annotates hits vs misses and the hit ratio over a time window. so you can tell if it's your prompt variability causing misses. also there's a little badge that says "prefix-cache: 0 hits".
01:45 - Tom: sometimes our SRE sees occasional long tail latency even when cache hit rate is decent. what else should we look at?
01:52 - Diego: look at the playback and debug flow. i'll switch to playback — this replays the same request across different model variants or with different runtime params. we used this to reproduce a flakey failure for another customer.
02:06 - Diego: starting playback now — selecting model variant: "redwood-rl-3-small" then "rl-3-quant" for cost tier fallback. watch token-level latencies change.
02:20 - Maya: oh that's neat, so we can compare model variants side-by-side and see how token emission latency differs.
02:26 - Diego: exactly. also note we can introduce a KV cache warmup in playback to see effect on first-byte latency vs subsequent tokens.
02:34 - Aisha: quick aside — Maya, curious about your success criteria for this debugging flow? is it reducing MTTD or preventing customer-seen errors?
02:42 - Maya: both. MTTD down to under 5 minutes for ops triage would be amazing. also we need a reliable way to root-cause if an utterance produced hallucination vs a model regression.
02:52 - Diego: Console supports annotations on traces, you can pin prompts and link to evals. for hallucination vs regression we tie traces back to prompt bank and recent model rollouts.
03:03 - Priya: and how do rollouts show up?
03:06 - Diego: rollout metadata is on the trace header; you can see which model version and any canary flags. if a canary was active for that request, Console shows it and you can filter traces by rollout.
03:18 - Jared: security — if we do Private VPC, where are audit logs stored? we need retention controls and KMS integration.
03:24 - Aisha: good point. we will share SOC2 docs but brief answer: audit logs can be shipped to your cloud account or stored in Redwood-managed encrypted buckets with optional bring-your-own-KMS. for Private we support customer-managed keys and network egress restrictions.
03:39 - Jared: does Request Inspector expose anything PII-ish? any redaction?
03:43 - Diego: by default traces capture metadata and token timing but not full user PII unless you enable verbose mode. there are configurable redaction rules and token masking; we'll include the redaction doc in the packet.
03:55 - Maya: can you show a case where fallback saved the user flow?
03:58 - Diego: yep — playback of a recent incident: initial primary model timed out at token 12 due to a memory pressure, Console automatically retried to a smaller quantized variant per the fallback policy. you can see in the trace tree: request -> model timeout span -> automatic fallback -> success. the Console highlights the automatic fallback reason and latency delta.
04:20 - Elena: is that automatic or do we have to configure it?
04:23 - Diego: you configure a policy per route: latency threshold, error types that trigger fallback, and allowed fallback variants. we ship sane defaults but teams tune them.
04:33 - Tom: network retries between our app and Redwood could also manifest similarly right?
04:36 - Diego: yes. which is why trace context includes network hops and region data. you can break down timing by client->edge->model.
04:45 - Priya: what's the best practice for KV prefixing? we're trying to cache conversation history snippets but have many user-specific tokens.
04:52 - Diego: prefixing should be coarse-grained: cache shared system prompts and frequently-reused leading prompts, avoid per-user entirely unless you're okay with low hit rates. Console's cache heatmap helps identify which prefixes yield hits. we also suggest a TTL strategy: TTL of 1h for conversational system prompts, shorter for volatile user inputs.
05:14 - Maya: will Optimize give recommendations for cache settings?
05:17 - Diego: yes, Optimize analyzes request patterns and suggests batching, prefixing and quantization profiles. it's not prescriptive but gives a delta estimate in tokens and %-cost.
05:25 - Aisha: can we demo a short "MTTD drill" — find a failure, triage, and produce remediation?
05:29 - Diego: sure i'll walk through a synthetic. opening trace list, filtering status: 5xx + latency>1s. clicking top one.
05:37 - Diego: timestamp 00:00 shows request start; at 00:18 there's an error span: "model-inference: error code 503". look at logs attached: gc spike on node, memory pressure, then retry. playback shows if we replay with a warmed cache we remove 200ms from cold-start.
05:56 - Tom: can we attach our internal metrics to that trace (datadog/grafana)?
06:00 - Diego: yes you can ingests tags and custom span ids. Console supports linking to external dashboards; we can include Datadog trace ids in metadata so you can pivot from your dashboards to Redwood trace.
06:11 - Elena: about token-level cost. i see a breakdown, is the token counting aligned with what we'll be billed?
06:16 - Aisha: yes the Console token breakdown mirrors billing units for Hosted. for Dedicated you'll get the same breakdown but billing is via committed capacity. Optimize can show estimated cost per route.
06:27 - Priya: On canaries and model rollbacks — if a regression is detected by our eval set, can Console auto-roll back?
06:33 - Diego: we don't auto-roll back without explicit policy. but Console supports configurable regression alerts tied to eval sets; you can set auto-fallback to a stable variant while you investigate.
06:45 - Maya: one of our worries is too many false positives from playback, any way to sandbox?
06:50 - Diego: Playback has a sandbox toggle and you can enable dry-run mode which executes everything in a non-billable test pool. useful for tuning fallbacks and cache warmups.
06:59 - Aisha: okay quick pause — jared any last compliance Qs before we continue?
07:03 - Jared: just confirm retention windows and ability to burn data on request. also SSO via SAML is mandatory.
07:10 - Aisha: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported; retention windows configurable and we have deletion APIs for purge requests. we'll attach network and retention docs.
07:20 - Diego: continuing — i'll show the trace heatmap: you can select a span and see a distribution of latencies across the fleet. this is great to spot outliers.
07:33 - Diego: notice this spike cluster at 800ms that correlates to a certain hardware region. you can then route requests away or label them for deeper infra analysis.
07:44 - Tom: could that be a specific kernel or nv driver issue?
07:47 - Diego: potentially, which is why we include kernel/build metadata when available. for Private on-prem installs we also allow deeper host-level telemetry collection.
07:59 - Maya: what's the lead time to get dedicated capacity?
08:03 - Aisha: typically 2-4 weeks for reserved pools depending on size and region; private/VPC onboarding is longer — usually 4-8 weeks with security review.
08:12 - Priya: alright can we look at a recent customer example where playback found a subtle prompt tokenization issue?
08:18 - Diego: demo: playback showed that trailing non-breaking spaces changed tokenization, causing a mismatch in kv keys, which led to misses. Console displays the raw prompt bytes and tokenization diff so you can see that invisible char.
08:32 - Elena: that would have been impossible to find quickly without token-level views.
08:36 - Diego: exactly. next i'll show how to annotate and file an incident: within a trace you can create an investigation ticket that links to the trace and automatically tags affected routes and users.
08:49 - Diego: create incident now -> fill summary -> assign to Tom. Done. this will populate a webhook to your slack channel if you set it.
08:59 - Tom: great. how about alerting thresholds?
09:02 - Diego: thresholds are per-route and per-model; you can set error rate SLOs and token-latency p95 thresholds. Console will surface when thresholds are breached and include representative traces.
09:12 - Maya: for the pilot we want Redwood to run a focused run: 48h of playback across our top 50 prompts, capture hit rates, and recommend cache settings. is that something you do?
09:23 - Aisha: yes we offer a Pilot package — Redwood SE + AE will run that with you, we'll produce a small report and recommendations. i'll include scope in the next email.
09:33 - Priya: do you need any credentials for playback? we won't share prod keys.
09:37 - Diego: we can replay against a scrubbed data set or use masked tokens; we also support a safe sandboxes for playback that don't require prod keys.
09:44 - Jared: about encryption at rest for trace logs?
09:47 - Diego: all logs encrypted at rest; for Private you can bring your own KMS and we support HSM-backed keys. we'll include the KMS integration guide.
09:57 - Aisha: wrapping up with a demo of a simple remediation — adjust cache TTL and re-run playback. changing prefix TTL from 1h to 4h increases hit rate from 12% to 48% in this synthetic example, see the cost delta estimate in Optimize panel.
10:14 - Elena: that level of visibility and the estimate is exactly what our product team needs to pitch to finance.
10:19 - Maya: last question — does Console keep a lineage between requests and the eval results used to approve models?
10:24 - Diego: yes traces can link back to eval buckets; Console will show which eval triggers fired. if a regression alert fires, you can pivot to the exact prompt set.
10:33 - Aisha: ok let's capture next steps (we'll also drop these in email). Diego, can you run the playback session for HarborCare next week?
10:40 - Diego: yes i'll schedule and prepare scripts.
10:42 - Aisha: Maya/Tom you'll send 2-3 trace ids and the top 50 prompt list, jared send your compliance checklist. we'll get the SOC2 + KMS + network diagrams over by friday.
10:52 - Maya: noted. thanks.
10:55 - Aisha: awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the packet and a pilot scope.
11:00 - Meeting end.

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker label mismatches; some accents caused minor word swaps (e.g., "qc" heard as "k-c"). Console UI elements may be paraphrased.
